DT01-q01-j4cpxq: The first trailer swings the least; crack-the-whip makes the last trailer most likely to turn over.
The swing grows toward the back, so the last trailer, not the middle, is most at risk.
DT01-q02-305ls5: No endorsement makes triples legal in California; they are not allowed at all.
Triples are not legal anywhere in California, freeways included.
DT01-q03-3iw9u9: The lighter trailer goes in the rear; the heavier one goes first for the safest handling.
Age does not decide the order; the more heavily loaded trailer goes first.
DT01-q04-k8vk6c: ABS helps control; it is not why doubles roll over. Crack-the-whip is.
Doubles have extra dead axles, not drive axles; crack-the-whip makes them roll over.
DT01-q05-oi94cm: A speed safe for a single-trailer rig may be too fast for less stable doubles.
Doubles need slower curve speeds, not momentum; steer gently and go slowly.
DT01-q06-p1b098: The trailers do have brakes; the problem is length and dead axles the drive axles must pull.
ABS on dollies helps control; skids come from length and extra dead axles.
DT01-q07-v7fr6s: The rule is to avoid spots you cannot pull straight through, not to back in.
The trailer hand valve is not a parking brake; the rule is to pick spots you can pull through.
DT01-q08-4roj55: The 1998 rule requires anti-lock brakes, not spring brakes on both axles.
The dolly ABS lamp is yellow and on the left side, not red on the right.
DT01-q09-u0nd59: The service line and pedal don't set the trailer's emergency brakes; charging then disconnecting the emergency line does.
Leaving wheels free lets it roll; set the emergency brakes and chock if in doubt.
DT01-q10-n8flj3: Shut-off valves close air lines; dolly brakes release by opening the air tank petcock.
The red knob sends air from the tractor; a loose dolly is released by opening its petcock.
DT01-q11-ao1kx1: Too high is wrong; it should sit slightly lower so the dolly lifts it slightly as it goes under.
It should sit slightly lower than the fifth wheel center, not level with it.
DT01-q12-arxasl: Raise it completely only later, after the hookups; first raise it slightly.
Raise it slightly right away, then completely before driving, never leaving it down.
DT01-q13-jd8vyz: Open valves at the last trailer's rear let air escape; they must be closed.
This is reversed: open at the rear of the first trailer, closed at the rear of the second.
DT01-q14-z5befd: You open that valve to check air; no air means something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
The petcock should be closed, but no air at the back still means something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
DT01-q15-qw962t: Park in a straight line, not at an angle, on firm, level ground.
A downgrade could let the trailer roll; use firm, level ground in a straight line.
DT01-q16-xf1czo: The handbook's reason is the tow bar: it may fly up and injure someone, and recoupling gets very hard.
The dolly air tank is not the danger; the tow bar may fly up and injure someone.
DT01-q17-m8bkih: This is a real uncoupling step, so it is not the exception.
This is a real uncoupling step, so it is not the exception.
DT01-q18-5u2mgu: The first trailer comes off last; uncouple the third trailer first.
The second trailer comes off after the third; start with the third trailer.
DT01-q19-14j975: Jaws around the head are wrong; they must close around the shank of the kingpin.
The glide plate is part of the upper fifth wheel; the jaws lock around the kingpin shank.
DT01-q20-3lajy6: Opening the petcock only releases dolly brakes when moving it by hand; for driving it must be closed.
The dolly air tank drain valve must be fully closed; the handbook allows no partly open setting.
DT01-q21-b4p818: Checking that the pintle hook is latched is a real doubles check.
Checking that safety chains are secured is a real doubles check.
DT01-q22-av6vaz: Trailer ride height is not the issue; too far forward risks frame and cab strikes in turns.
Jaw position is checked at the kingpin shank; a slide too far forward risks frame or cab strikes in turns.
DT01-q23-p4man5: The yellow knob is the tractor parking brake; the red knob sends air to the trailers.
Draining tanks lowers pressure; the check needs the red trailer air supply knob pushed in.
DT01-q24-f85u0a: The tractor protection valve is not what must be on; the trailer handbrake or brake pedal is.
The dolly parking brake does not send air; the service line needs the handbrake or pedal on.
DT01-q25-gvmkns: Crossed lines are not the handbook's first check; check that the shut-off valves are open.
The tractor parking brake holds the rig for the test; check the shut-off valves are open.
DT01-q26-rroi6o: [CA] No skills test is given for the endorsement; do not bring doubles to the Class A test.
[CA] There is no doubles skills test; the endorsement is knowledge test only.
